verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 892 (printed 868) shows Figure D.9 as a flowchart: Evaluate condition-1 -> 'Condition-1 true' decision; 'yes' exits right on a line that runs down to the arrow 'Truth value is true'; 'no' goes down to Evaluate condition-2 -> 'Condition-2 false'; 'yes' exits left down to the arrow 'Truth value is false'; 'no' goes down to Evaluate condition-3 -> 'Condition-3 false'; 'yes' exits left joining the false line, 'no' exits right joining the true line. The claim's pdf_says matches this exactly. The markdown keeps every box and label text but no edges or arrows: the decision outcomes are loose 'yes'/'no' words and the two terminals are recast as a two-column table, so the routing of each branch to a truth value (the figure's whole content: condition-2 AND condition-3 evaluated as a unit, condition-1 true short-circuiting to true) must be guessed from word order. Condition-1's 'yes' is not even tied to a direction. This is lost figure content, not furniture or wrapping. The figure is in informative Annex D, so severity structural (not normative) is right.
